title: Red Callender's Sextet at Lai Yi Chai's
summary: He leads a multi-ethnic six-piece band at a Chinese restaurant run by Tats Matsuo while playing with the symphony.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, that wiped it out. No, I stayed. The rest of the guys came back. Trummy stayed until he went with Louis years later. So I stayed, and then I came back and I decided to go back; I went back and played with the symphony. I stayed with the symphony for about three years, and meanwhile I had my own band, working at Lai Yi Chai's, which was probably the hippest Chinese restaurant you ever saw, run by Japanese. Tats Matsuo was the owner of Lai Yi Chai's, and I formed a six-piece band, which I called the "Biggest Little Band in the World," and they called Red Callender's Sextet. My piano player was Filipino, my alto player was Chinese, my tenor player was Hawaiian-Chinese, my
drummer was full Chinese, and the trumpet player was Korean. So I was the only brother in the band.
